subject: Getting information about a ggplot object

messages.author: 3033a60610caec0b
messages.subject: Getting information about a ggplot object
parts:
Does anyone know how you can get information about a ggplot object?
The specific information I'm looking for is the x-range and y-range
for a histogram plot. As this changes based on the value of binwidth,
it can't be known from the raw data underlying the plot. This
information will be used for placing text on the plot.

Ideally the code will look something like,

jj <- qplot(x = values, data = test.data, geom = "histogram")

xrange <- [insert code here]
yrange <- [insert code here]

jj + geom_text(x = xrange[2], y = yrange[2], aes(label = label), data
= label.data)

Thanks,
Brandon

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Getting information about a ggplot object
parts:
Hi Brandon,

This information doesn't exist until the plot is actually drawn - you
can change the data up until the last minute so it can't be
precomputed. However, it's not hard to get the x ranges yourself:

rng <- c(
round_any(min(test.data$values), binwidth, floor),
round_any(max(test.data$values), binwidth, ceiling)
)

Alternatively, if you want both the x and y ranges, use the bin()
function which powers the histogram in ggplot2.

Hadley

parts:
I am not sure I understand this. What is clearly meant is being able
to get some information from an object, as if the object had been
drawn just then. That is clearly a unique entity. It might be very
hard to get at, of course.

Functionality as this would be very nice for customization. It would
even be ok if the plot had to be created in order for the information
to be extracted.

An example: I recently had to modify a rather complex graph with many
facets and a color(Dataset). I needed to enhance the color for one
particular value of Dataset. In the end I had to re-engineer the
ggplot2 color scale (because I did like the color scale for the other
Datasets), figuring out how the colors are chosen if the are X
different values of Dataset, and managed to create a manual scale.

But that would have been much easier if a call like
extractColorscale(qqplot(...))
would be possible.


Kasper
